title: Polynomials and the Factor Theorem
seo_title: Year 12 A Level Maths: Polynomials Worksheets
standard_text: Manipulate polynomials algebraically, including expanding brackets and collecting like terms, factorisation and simple algebraic division; use of the factor theorem.
meta_desc: Free Year 12 A level maths worksheets on polynomials: algebraic division, the factor theorem, the remainder theorem and factorising cubics fully. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: If f(a) = 0, then (x − a) is a factor of f(x).
key_sub: Divide by the factor to find the quadratic, then factorise again.
body_html:
How it works

The factor theorem: (x − a) is a factor of f(x) exactly when f(a) = 0. The remainder when f(x) is divided by (x − a) is f(a).

Example

Show (x − 2) is a factor of x³ − 8.

f(2) = 8 − 8 = 0

Answer: it is a factor

Example

Factorise x³ − 7x + 6 fully.

f(1) = 0

Divide: x² + x − 6

Answer: (x − 1)(x − 2)(x + 3)

Common mistakes

  • Using f(2) to test (x + 2). Use f(−2).
  • Stopping after one factor.
  • Sign errors in the division.

items.q: Factorise 2x³ − 2x² + 2x − 2 by grouping.
items.e: Group the first two and last two terms: x²(2x − 2) + 1(2x − 2). The common factor is (2x − 2): (2x − 2)(x² + 1).

items.q: Factorise 3x³ + 5x² + 6x + 10 by grouping.
items.e: Group the first two and last two terms: x²(3x + 5) + 2(3x + 5). The common factor is (3x + 5): (3x + 5)(x² + 2).

items.q: Factorise x³ − 2x² − 3x + 6 by grouping.

items.q: Factorise 2x³ − 4x² − 8x + 16 by grouping completely.
items.e: Group: x²(2x − 4) − 4(2x − 4) = (2x − 4)(x² − 4). Then x² − 4 is a difference of squares: (2x − 4)(x − 2)(x + 2).
